chunks: Yūnus, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Intentional killing is that in which one strikes with a weapon or a stick and does not desist from it until he is killed; and accidental killing is that which he did not intend."

key_terms.الْخَطَأُ: mistake or accidental act, here meaning unintentional killing
key_terms.الْعَصَا: the stick or staff, another instrument of striking
key_terms.اَلْعَمْدُ: intentional action, here meaning deliberate killing
key_terms.بِالسِّلَاحِ: with a weapon, indicating a means typically used in deliberate harm
key_terms.يَضْرِبُ: he strikes or beats, indicating the act of assault
key_terms.يُقْلِعُ: he desists or stops, here referring to ceasing the assault

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام distinguish intentional killing from accidental killing?
ai.summary: This hadith defines the distinction between intentional and accidental killing in the context of diyat and qisas. It identifies intentional killing by continued assault with a weapon or stick until death occurs, while accidental killing is described as that which is not done deliberately.
